title: SLO program collaboration plan - Q2 2026
body:
Purpose:
This is a working cross-functional plan for the SLO and reliability program we need to push through in Q2 2026. It captures scope, owners, milestones, measurement design, rollout strategy, and the minimum runbook/alerting changes required for initial pilots.

Context / problem statement:
- We have inconsistent SLO coverage across hosted-api routes and Dedicated endpoints. Some services have vague targets, others have none.
- Alerts are noisy (page storms during transient infra events) and not tied to customer-impacting SLO breaches.
- Product teams lack a simple path to agree SLO targets and trace SLIs to user-visible impact.
- We need an operational program that reduces P0s from model-serving regressions and gives product teams a predictable way to manage reliability tradeoffs.

Program goals (Q2 measurable):
1) Establish canonical SLO definitions for the top 12 production routes (hosted + dedicated) that represent ~85% of user requests.
2) Deploy SLO monitoring dashboards and daily SLI backfills for those routes.
3) Reduce pages triggered by infra-only token spikes by 40% by tuning alerting windows and adding synthetic canaries.
4) Run two cross-functional SLO review cycles with Product, Platform, and Customer Success to land targets and runbooks.

Scope (what's in / out):
- In: HTTP generation/chat endpoints, embeddings endpoints, model routing service, dedicated GPU pool ingress.
- Out: internal admin/ops-only endpoints, archived experiments, non-production clusters.

Stakeholders & roles:
- SRE (program lead): Maya Chen (owner) — overall program management, measurement platform changes, alerts rewiring.
- Platform/Serving runtime: Ethan Morales — implement metric hooks (latency buckets, success codes, queue time).
- Product (hosted-api): Priya Kapoor — define user impact tiers, approve targets for hosted routes.
- Product (dedicated): Diego Alvarez — agree on Dedicated-specific SLOs (throughput/availability).
- Observability: Hannah Lee — dashboards, synthetic canaries, SLI calculation pipelines.
- Customer Success: Jordan Patel — customer communication plan, identify customer-critical routes and SLAs.
- Security/Compliance (advisory): Linh Tran — ensure metrics and logs follow PII rules.

High-level timeline (milestones):
- Week 0 (Feb 23–27): Kickoff + inventory of routes and current metrics. Deliverable: route inventory spreadsheet.
- Week 1–2 (Mar 1–13): Define SLI candidates for each route + measurement method doc. Deliverable: slo-definitions.md (draft).
- Week 3 (Mar 14–20): Prototype SLI pipeline and dashboards for 4 pilot routes. Deliverable: dashboards + backfilled 30 days.
- Week 4 (Mar 21–27): Alert policy draft and runbook templates. Deliverable: alerting playbook v0.
- Week 5–6 (Mar 28–Apr 10): Cross-functional review cycle #1 (hosted pilot). Deliverable: agreed targets and runbooks for hosted pilot routes.
- Week 7–9 (Apr 11–May 1): Dedicated pilot + A/B of alert sensitivity changes. Deliverable: dedicated SLOs + tuned thresholds.
- Week 10–12 (May 2–22): Rollout to remaining top-12 routes, training sessions for product/oncall. Deliverable: SLO catalog and public runbooks.
- End of Q2 (Jun 30): Program retrospective and handoff to runbook owners. Deliverable: program report + next-phase proposal.

SLO tiers and candidate targets (examples, for discussion):
- Tier 1 (critical user-facing): p99 latency < 1.2s, availability 99.95% monthly. Affects interactive chat/generation short prompts.
- Tier 2 (important background/embeddings): p95 latency < 0.6s, availability 99.9% monthly.
- Tier 3 (low-risk batch/reranking): p99 latency < 5s, availability 99.5% monthly.
Note: exact numbers are drafts — use the Q2 review cycles to firm them up per route.

Designing SLIs (guidance + constraints):
- Prefer user-centric SLIs: e.g., model-response-latency end-to-end (ingress -> egress, including queue time).
- Instrument success as 2xx with non-empty completion tokens (for generation endpoints) or well-formed embedding vectors.
- Avoid relying solely on host-level CPU/GPU metrics for SLI — use them only as supporting telemetry.
- Backfill data for at least 30 days to understand seasonality and tail behavior before finalizing SLOs.

Alerting strategy to reduce noise:
- Move from immediate p99 alerting to "SLO windowed" alerts: e.g., pages only when 10m error budget burn rate exceeds threshold AND sustained for 5m.
- Introduce multi-level signals: P0 (SLO breach imminent), P1 (degraded but not yet breach), Informational.
- Correlate infra signals (GPU OOMs, node drain) and automatically create incidents as "infrastructure degraded" with different routing to infra-oncall.
- Use suppression rules when rolling deployments are recognized via rollout tags from CI.

Runbooks & playbooks (minimum viable):
- Each SLO must have a one-page runbook with: owner, what the SLI measures, how to query current SLI, common causes, immediate triage steps, mitigation (fallback models, route to cheaper variants), escalation path.
- Template to include a check-list: "is there a model-fallback in routing?" "are caches warm?" "is KV store healthy?"

Measurement platform changes required:
- Add latency histograms with consistent boundaries (us, ms) across services.
- Emit a per-request trace id and an SLI-friendly tag indicating route/prompt-type.
- Observability team to create canonical SLI query library (prebuilt SQL/PromQL snippets) and store SLO config in git (slo-definitions repo).

Rollout plan (phased & safe):
- Phase A (pilot): 4 hosted routes where product risk is lowest and instrumentation is complete. Use synthetic canaries + live SLI.
- Phase B (hosted top-12): roll to remaining hosted routes once pilot stabilizes.
- Phase C (Dedicated pools): coordinate with Dedicated infra to account for capacity guarantees and distinct failure modes.
- During all phases: have a rollback plan to revert alert sensitivity if pages increase.

Customer communication and contractual considerations:
- CS to create a customer-facing FAQ for SLOs vs SLA differences.
- For Dedicated customers with contractual SLAs, SLO targets must be translated to contractual language and reviewed with Legal.

Success metrics (what we will measure at program completion):
- % of top-12 routes with production SLOs and runbooks (target 100%).
- Reduction in pages per 1,000 requests (target -40% for infra-related storms).
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for SLO-impacting incidents improved by 25%.
- Product satisfaction: post-rollout survey with product/oncall showing >=4/5 confidence in SLO program.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: SLOs set too conservatively leading to constant breaches. Mitigation: use conservative alerting windows, runbook mitigations, and gradual tightening.
- Risk: Instrumentation gaps across services. Mitigation: block rollout on missing core metrics and provide a low-friction instrumentation checklist.
- Risk: Paging increases during rollout due to discovery of real issues. Mitigation: use pilot phases, schedule rollouts in low-traffic windows, and apply temporary alert suppressions.

Open questions (requires cross-team discussion):
- Should we count quota/ratelimit throttles as errors for SLI on a per-route basis? Product input needed.
- How to surface model-quality regressions (hallucination/semantic drift) as part of reliability program — measurement approach? (research/product).
- What is the canonical SLO config format — YAML in repo, Confluence table, or managed in the Observability product?

Next steps (this week):
- Owner (Maya): finalize route inventory and assign per-route product owner meetings (due Mar 2).
- Observability (Hannah): prototype dashboard for 2 pilot routes and send access to reviewers (due Mar 9).
- Platform (Ethan): implement one latency histogram and a request tag in dev cluster to validate pipeline (due Mar 9).
- Product (Priya & Diego): workshop to prioritize top-12 routes for SLO coverage (Mar 4).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Attach sample SLO YAML after first review.
- Save a copy of the route inventory to the slo-definitions repo.
- Schedule two 60-min review sessions (one for hosted, one for dedicated).

Appendix A — Quick example SLO YAML (draft):

service: hosted-api-generation
slo_name: p99-latency-availability
objective: "p99 latency < 1.2s over 30d AND availability >= 99.95% monthly"
slis:
  - name: p99_latency
    query: "histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(latency_bucket[30d])) by (le))"
    type: latency
    window: 30d
  - name: availability
    query: "1 - sum(rate(request_errors_total[30d])) / sum(rate(requests_total[30d]))"
    type: ratio
    window: 30d
owners: ["hosted-api-product", "eng-sre"]

(That YAML will be refined and stored in the slo-definitions repo.)

End of draft. Feedback welcome — especially on SLI design constraints and alerting thresholds.
